traps: GAAP vs adjusted: reported earnings of $12.1 billion ($6.11) are GAAP; adjusted earnings of $12.0 billion ($6.06) are non-GAAP and come in below reported this quarter because special items (an asset sale gain of $230 million in international downstream less pension settlement costs of $86 million after tax, 113 pre-tax) were a net $144 million benefit while foreign currency effects, a separate adjustment, cost $49 million.

Timing effects: reported earnings include $1.4 billion of favorable timing effects (derivative mark-to-market and LIFO), about 12 percent of reported earnings (computed); these are not special items and remain in adjusted earnings, so they lift both reported earnings ($12.1 billion) and adjusted EPS ($6.06).

Quarter vs sequential vs year to date: the summary tables carry 2Q26, 1Q26, 2Q25, YTD 2026 and YTD 2025 columns; 1Q26 was weak (earnings 2,210, downstream loss of (817), free cash flow of (1.5)), so a sequential comparison is not the year-over-year one.
Units: summary earnings are in $ MM, cash flow and capex in $ B, production in MBOED (thousands of barrels of oil-equivalent per day), natural gas in MMCFD; Attachments are in millions of dollars.

Cash flow labels: CFFO of $22.6 billion is GAAP; CFFO excluding working capital ($19.7 billion), free cash flow ($18.1 billion) and adjusted free cash flow ($15.4 billion) are non-GAAP; CFFO includes a favorable working capital effect of 2,945 (Attachment 3), which is context, not a required part of the CFFO fact.

Buybacks: the Shares repurchased row (3,117) carries footnote (1), which says it includes excise tax payments for prior-year repurchases ($114 million in 2026); '$3.1 billion of share repurchases' is the accepted phrasing, and cash dividends paid (3,504) is a cash flow line, not the $1.78 declared dividend.
Segment vs total: Upstream 8,182 = U.S. 3,541 + International 4,641; Downstream 4,868 = U.S. 2,411 + International 2,457; All Other net charges were (978), roughly flat with (974).
Revenue: the release prints no revenue growth rate; sales and other operating revenues are 67,199 versus 44,375, and total revenues and other income are 70,055 versus 44,822.

Production: the 20 percent worldwide growth is largely legacy Hess; the record is U.S. production (2,077 MBOED, up 382,000 barrels per day); international growth was partly offset by Partitioned Zone curtailments tied to the Middle East conflict.

Against the trend: international downstream refinery crude inputs fell 10 percent and refined product sales fell 13 percent on Middle East supply disruptions; U.S. refined product sales fell 4 percent; U.S. natural gas realization dropped to $0.91 per MCF from $1.75.
ROCE: 21.4 is the quarter on annualized earnings; 13.0 is year to date; the headline rounds to 21 percent.
Refining: U.S. refinery crude unit throughput was a record 1.07 million barrels per day at more than 97 percent utilization; the headline bullet says 97 percent.

No guidance: the production fact (f06) fills the outlook core slot because the release gives none; the release points to a separate Sensitivities and Forward Guidance document on the website; the $3-4 billion structural cost reduction program by end of 2026 is a cost target, and the $3 billion and $1.5 billion Hess synergy figures are annual run-rate savings achieved, not in-quarter earnings effects.

Microsoft: Chevron signed an agreement to develop a West Texas power facility providing approximately 2.67 gigawatts of behind-the-meter capacity under a 20-year power purchase agreement; it is signed, not operating, and no financial terms are disclosed.

Deals not closed: the Iraq heads of agreement cover potential participation only, and the Singapore Refining Company sale is expected to close in 2027; only the Hong Kong fuels and lubricants sale was completed.
Commodity context: Brent averaged $104 per barrel versus $68 a year ago and $81 in 1Q26; do not present it as Chevron's realized price (U.S. liquids realization was $70.80, international $96.41).
